source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What are the main classes of biomolecules? Give one function of each.
questions.solution: **Carbohydrates:** energy source (glucose, starch). **Proteins:** enzymes and structure (haemoglobin, collagen). **Lipids:** energy storage and membranes (fats, phospholipids). **Nucleic acids:** genetic information (DNA, RNA).
questions.knowledgeNote: Carbohydrates ≈ (CH₂O)n; proteins are amino-acid polymers — composition formulas both get tested.

questions.question: Describe the structure of a nucleotide and explain its role in DNA.
questions.solution:
A **nucleotide** = pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA) + nitrogenous base (A/T/G/C) + phosphate.

Nucleotides polymerise into strands; two strands coil into the double helix via complementary pairing (A–T, G–C) — the pairing rules that copy genetic information faithfully.
questions.knowledgeNote: Sugar + base alone is a nucleoside; add phosphate and it becomes a nucleotide.

questions.question: Describe the salient features of the Watson-Crick model of DNA.
questions.solution: (1) Two antiparallel polynucleotide strands coiled into a **double helix**. (2) Sugar–phosphate backbone outside, bases inside. (3) Complementary pairing: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds). (4) Diameter ~20 Å with one full turn per 34 Å (10 base pairs). (5) Right-handed helix.
questions.knowledgeNote: Chargaff's rules (A=T, G=C) were the data Watson and Crick built the model to fit.

questions.question: What are enzymes? Write any four of their properties.
questions.solution:
**Enzymes** are protein biocatalysts that speed reactions without being consumed.

(1) Highly specific (lock-and-key / induced fit). (2) Work best at optimum T and pH. (3) Needed in tiny amounts; reusable. (4) Lower activation energy. (5) Inhibited by poisons (cyanide, heavy metals).
questions.knowledgeNote: Apoenzyme (protein) + cofactor (metal/vitamin) = holoenzyme — the complete active form.

questions.question: Classify carbohydrates with one example of each class.
questions.solution: **Monosaccharides** (single sugars): glucose, fructose. **Oligosaccharides** (2–10 units): sucrose, maltose. **Polysaccharides** (many units): starch, cellulose, glycogen.
questions.knowledgeNote: Glucose = instant energy; starch/glycogen = storage; cellulose = structure — function follows polymerisation.

questions.question: Distinguish between saturated and unsaturated fatty acids. Why do phospholipids form bilayers in water?
questions.solution:
**Saturated** acids have only single bonds (straight chains, solid fats like ghee); **unsaturated** have C=C kinks (oils like mustard oil).

Phospholipids are amphipathic — hydrophilic heads face water on both sides while hydrophobic tails hide inside — so a **bilayer** is the lowest-energy arrangement, forming every cell membrane.
questions.knowledgeNote: The bilayer's fluid mosaic (Singer–Nicolson) explains selective permeability and membrane protein movement.
